title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the stable compactification \hat M_{0,I} of M_{0,I} for |I| = 5 (that is, \bar M_{0,5}, a smooth proper surface over Z, the quintic del Pezzo surface). The aim is to describe the boundary combinatorially.

Boundary components and points:
- The boundary divisors D_{I'} are indexed by the 2-subsets I' of I. There are 10 of them.
- Each D_{I'} is a P^1 carrying 3 special points.
- The boundary points (codimension 2 strata) are indexed by the 15 partitions of I of type (2,2,1).
- D_{I'} meets D_{I''} if and only if I' and I'' are disjoint (previous page).

Icosahedral translation (this page):
- Each 2-subset is replaced by its complementary 3-subset, a 'triangle' of I. The 10 triangles correspond to the 10 faces of the 'icosaèdre gauche', i.e. pairs of opposite faces of the ordinary icosahedron. In modern terms this is the hemi-icosahedron, the regular projective map {3,5}_5 with 6 vertices, 15 edges and 10 faces.
- A (2,2,1) partition is read as a 'square' structure on 4 of the 5 points, the two pairs being the diagonals. The 15 squares correspond to the 15 edges.
- Incidence: edge a lies on face f if and only if the complement of the triangle of f is one of the two diagonal pairs of the square of a. This is exactly the statement that the point D_{ij} ∩ D_{kl} lies on D_{ij}.
- So the incidence relation (boundary divisors, boundary points) of \hat M_{0,5} matches (faces, edges) of the hemi-icosahedron. By duality it matches (vertices, edges) of the hemi-dodecahedron.

Consequence (next page): the dual graph of the boundary curve is the 1-skeleton of the hemi-dodecahedron, which is the Petersen graph.

Margin note: begins assigning to each edge the 4 other edges of its two adjacent faces (a rhombus picture), apparently toward an edge-colouring argument. It is left incomplete.

Next page: the boundary is a split stable curve over Spec Z. The identification is equivariant only for G_I^+ (A_5, the rotation group of the map), not for all of S_5. Grothendieck flags that this should be understood through a 'bi-icosaèdre'.
errors: No mathematical error. The incidence criterion checks out: each face, with complementary pair {ij}, carries 3 edges (the three ways to pair off the remaining 3 points after choosing one partner pair). Each edge lies on 2 faces. Counts 10/15 and degree 3 match the Petersen graph.

The equivariance remark on the next page is correct. Aut(Petersen graph) = S_5, but the regular map (hemi-dodecahedron) has rotation group A_5. Odd permutations carry the 2-cell embedding to a second, mirror one, which explains the 'bi-icosaèdre' remark.

ideas.what: The boundary of \bar M_{0,5} has 10 divisors and 15 nodes; its dual graph is the Petersen graph (Kneser graph K(5,2)).
ideas.modern_name: Petersen graph as boundary complex / tropical M_{0,5}; the 10 lines of the quintic del Pezzo
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for the lines on the dP5; in moduli language standard since Keel/Kapranov (1990s) and tropical geometry (Speyer–Sturmfels 2004)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,5} and the Teichmüller tower in general terms, not this explicit combinatorics

ideas.what: Identification of this incidence structure with faces/edges of the hemi-icosahedron and, dually, vertices/edges of the hemi-dodecahedron, via an orientation of I (A_5 = icosahedral rotation group).
ideas.modern_name: Petersen graph = 1-skeleton of the hemi-dodecahedron (regular projective map {5,3}_5)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Known in polytope/map theory (Coxeter, regular maps); the link to \bar M_{0,5} is folklore

ideas.what: Encoding (2,2,1) partitions as 'square structures' (diagonal pairs) on 4 of the 5 points.

missed.claim: The boundary of \bar M_{0,5}, viewed as a split stable curve over Spec Z, is an arithmetic-genus-6 stable curve: 10 rational components, 15 nodes, Petersen dual graph, b_1 = 6. It lies in |-2K| of the dP5. Grothendieck relates its symmetries (A_5 versus S_5) to a 'bi-icosahedron', i.e. the two chiral hemi-dodecahedral embeddings swapped by odd permutations. The arithmetic viewpoint, placing this maximally degenerate curve in \bar M_6 with its icosahedral A_5 structure, is a minor detail rarely spelled out.
missed.quote: la relation d'incidence des diviseurs à l'infini de la structure \hat M_{0,5} ... celle des faces et arêtes de l'icosaèdre gauche, et par dualité, à celle des sommets et des arêtes du dodécaèdre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly a pedagogical or folklore point. It links the Teichmüller-tower base case to regular maps, which could feed Galois–Teichmüller computations with the A_5-action on the boundary. It is not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The Petersen-graph boundary of \bar M_{0,5} is well known, and its realisation as the hemi-dodecahedron is folklore. Grothendieck's own twist (the hemi-icosahedron via triangles, the A_5 vs S_5 chirality, 'bi-icosaèdre') is a nice unpublished detail but not a new result.
